name: PlumHound - BloodHound Reporting and Pathfinding
description: PlumHound runs curated Cypher queries against a BloodHound neo4j database and produces blue/purple-team HTML reports: shortest paths to Domain Admins, Kerberoastable users, unconstrained delegation, stale accounts, and dozens more. Turns BloodHound graph data into actionable, reportable findings without manual Cypher.
notes:
=== PREREQUISITE ===
  # BloodHound data already ingested into neo4j (via SharpHound/bloodhound-python)

=== RUN DEFAULT TASK LIST (full report set) ===
  python3 PlumHound.py -s "bolt://127.0.0.1:7687" -u neo4j -p bloodhound -x tasks/default.tasks
  # HTML reports land in reports/

=== EASY MODE (one path report) ===
  python3 PlumHound.py -s "bolt://127.0.0.1:7687" -u neo4j -p bloodhound --easy

=== SINGLE CYPHER QUERY ===
  python3 PlumHound.py -s "bolt://127.0.0.1:7687" -u neo4j -p bloodhound \
    -c "MATCH (u:User {hasspn:true}) RETURN u.name" --title Kerberoastable

=== USEFUL BUILT-IN TASKS ===
  - Shortest paths to Domain Admins
  - Users with DCSync rights
  - Unconstrained/constrained delegation
  - Kerberoastable + AS-REP roastable accounts
  - Computers where Domain Users can RDP/admin
  - Stale/never-logged-on accounts

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  GoodHound  # similar reporting, scores paths by "busiest"
  BloodHound raw Cypher  # manual queries in the UI

examples.label: Custom Cypher to HTML
examples.command: python3 PlumHound.py -s "bolt://127.0.0.1:7687" -u neo4j -p bloodhound -c "MATCH (u:User {hasspn:true}) RETURN u.name" --title Kerberoastable

recommended.note: PlumHound reads the neo4j DB that BloodHound populates.
SharpHound collects the data PlumHound reports on.
Hand-write Cypher for queries PlumHound tasks do not cover.

defense.why_it_works: PlumHound only queries a neo4j database already built from AD collection data. It performs no new domain activity - the detectable activity is the upstream SharpHound/bloodhound-python collection.
defense.impact: Rapid identification of all privilege-escalation paths and misconfigurations in the domain.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1069.002] No direct AD detection (offline graph queries). Detect the upstream collection: heavy LDAP/SAMR enumeration, SharpHound signatures.
defense.artifacts: neo4j query logs on the attacker/analyst host; upstream collection artifacts on the DC.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4662 ObjectType="*" 
| stats count by SubjectUserName, ObjectName
| where count > 100
defense.sentinel_kql:
IdentityQueryEvents
| summarize Queries=count() by AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where Queries > 200
defense.prevention: Reduce ACL attack surface (tier model, LAPS, remove dangerous ACEs); the report output is a remediation to-do list - action it. Detect SharpHound collection upstream.
